from.place: Proof paragraph 2, coherent finite coefficient adjunction before R lim: interpretation of relative dg categories in the derived enrichment. Sublemma: replace variable object spaces by discrete object sets before localizing at fully faithful essentially surjective functors (Gepner–Haugseng Theorem 5.3.17). Supporting fact: Proposition 5.3.16 (canonical localization pushout of Remark 5.3.13); Lemma 5.3.15; Proposition 5.3.16, first proof paragraph: pullback of the canonical localization pushout along the Cartesian fibration

title: Cartesian-fibration base change preserves pushouts of infinity-categories
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Inner fibration has the inner-horn lifting meaning of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. In this statement a Cartesian fibration $p:X\to Y$ means an inner fibration admitting a lift $x'\to x$ of every arrow $y'\to p(x)$ with specified target, such that for every $z\in X$ the square $\operatorname{Map}_X(z,x')\to\operatorname{Map}_X(z,x)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_Y(pz,y')\to\operatorname{Map}_Y(pz,px)$ is a homotopy pullback. Let $A,B,C,D$ be infinity-categories and let
$$\begin{matrix}A&\longrightarrow&B\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ C&\longrightarrow&D\end{matrix}$$
be a coherent pushout square in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. Let $p:E\to D$ be a Cartesian fibration. Then its base-change square
$$\begin{matrix}A\times_D E&\longrightarrow&B\times_D E\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ C\times_D E&\longrightarrow&E\end{matrix}$$
is a pushout in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, with all pullbacks taken in infinity-categories. All displayed categories and the finite diagrams are taken in one sufficiently large fixed universe; no fibration condition on the arrows of the original square is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1.3 and Corollary 3.3.1.4, together with the Joyal-model homotopy-pushout interpretation of a pushout in Cat_infinity (Section 4.2.4). This is the model-independent base-change consequence used in Gepner–Haugseng Proposition 5.3.16, first proof paragraph; its citation of HTT Corollary 2.4.4.5 alone omits the arbitrary-simplicial-set comparison. Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical theorem.
